column1: For a DAB entity backed by a SQL view, set source.type to {{c1::view}}.
column2:
The type tells DAB that the source object is a view. Set source.object to the schema-qualified name, and configure the fields that identify each result row.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0+, mark each column that identifies a SQL view row by setting its {{c1::primary-key}} flag in the entity's fields array.
column2:
Mark every field that participates in the key. If you migrate from source.key-fields to the fields array in DAB 2.0, do not keep both forms on the entity.
Review source

column1: For a DAB entity backed by a SQL procedure, set source.type to {{c1::stored-procedure}}.
column2:
This type tells DAB to invoke the named procedure rather than treat it as a table. Set source.object to the schema-qualified procedure name.
Review source

column1: The DAB permission action for invoking a stored procedure is {{c1::execute}}.
column2:
Execute authorizes calling the procedure through DAB. Read applies to reading rows from an entity such as a table or view. It is not the permission for a procedure call.
Review source

column1: If rest.methods is omitted for a DAB stored-procedure endpoint, its default HTTP method is {{c1::POST}}.
column2:
Without an explicit method list, DAB exposes the procedure through POST. Add GET to rest.methods if you want to allow query-string calls as well.
Review source

column1: A POST request to a DAB stored-procedure endpoint supplies its input parameters in the {{c1::JSON request body}}.
column2:
The JSON property names match the procedure parameters. For example, {"MinPrice":10} passes 10 to MinPrice. The parameter configuration can define defaults, not aliases.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0+, the preferred source.parameters format for naming procedure inputs and setting defaults is an {{c1::array of parameter objects}}.
column2:
Each object describes one input by name and can set its requirement and default. DAB still accepts the older dictionary syntax, but the object array is the preferred format in 2.0.
Review source

column1: For a DAB stored procedure that changes data, configure graphql.operation as {{c1::mutation}}.
column2:
Mutation puts the generated field under the GraphQL Mutation type. It describes the intended API use. The SQL procedure still determines which data actually changes.
Review source

column1: With default naming, DAB procedure entity GetProducts generates the GraphQL field {{c1::executeGetProducts}}.
column2:
The default prefix distinguishes a generated procedure field from a table collection. Pass the declared procedure inputs as arguments to that field.
Review source

column1: For Order to multiple OrderDetail entities, set DAB relationship cardinality to {{c1::many}}.
column2:
Cardinality describes how many target rows one source row can match. One order can have many details. The reverse direction from one detail to its order is a one relationship.
Review source

column1: A DAB relationship names its destination entity through the {{c1::target.entity}} property.
column2:
Use the destination entity name from the DAB configuration. For example, point to Customer, not dbo.Customers, when Customer is the entity that maps to that table.
Review source

column1: To join two DAB GraphQL entities through a junction table that is not an API entity, configure {{c1::linking.object}}.
column2:
The linking object names the junction table even when clients cannot query it as its own entity. Map its two sets of fields to the source and target so DAB can join across it.
Review source
